subject: Re: Zephyrus Labs — request for priority latency & availability pledge
messages:
From: Matt Chen <matt.chen@zephyrus.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-10T09:14:00Z
Subject: Priority latency & availability ask — Zephyrus pilot

Hi David,

Quick note from the Zephyrus side — the engineering team is preparing a public beta of our real-time inference product and we're evaluating vendors for a hard latency + availability commitment during launch week (expected Jan 10–17). Our non-negotiable asks: a P95 inference latency under 50ms for our embedding/chat route during peak windows and 99.995% availability for the same window (US region).

We understand that this is outside standard SLAs; we're prepared to sign up for a 3-month reserved capacity commitment and cover incremental costs, but we need a written, signed pledge (or an MSA addendum) to align our customers.

Can Redwood provide a feasibility confirmation and a draft SLA this week? If possible, we'd like estimated incremental monthly cost and runbook commitments (on-call coverage, escalation path) so our procurement and legal teams can review in parallel.

Attached: initial requirements doc (brief).

Thanks —
Matt Chen
Head of Infrastructure, Zephyrus Labs
[Attachment: zephyrus-requirements-brief.pdf (PDF)]

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-10T11:02:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Priority latency & availability ask — Zephyrus pilot

Team — forwarding Zephyrus's ask. TL;DR: they want p95 < 50ms for embeddings/chat and 99.995% availability during launch week, on dedicated/reserved capacity, willing to pay incremental. Procurement wants a draft SLA + runbook to review this week.

Asks:
- Aditya: can product/serving confirm technical feasibility and an execution plan (dedicated pool size, model variant choices, fallback behavior) by EOD 12/11? If we can't hit 50ms p95 realistically, propose an alternate commitment and measurable fallback.
- Grace/Marcus: outline ops requirements (standby capacity, on-call coverage, burn rate on reserved nodes) and a skeletal runbook we can share with Zephyrus. Include any constraints around KV cache priming and cold-starts.
- Laura: scope legal/contract asks — SOC2 addendum, audit logs, data handling, and an estimate for redline turnaround.
- Neha: any CS/AM considerations (credits, onboarding support, day-of escalation) we should surface to procurement.

I'll keep Zephyrus in the loop but want internal alignment first. Attaching their brief and a perf sim template — pls add any files you produce to this thread.

Thanks,
David
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: zephyrus-requirements-brief.pdf (PDF)]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-11T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Priority latency & availability ask — Zephyrus pilot

Quick technical note from product/serving:
- Feasibility: Achievable if we run a dedicated GPU pool pinned to a trimmed model variant (8-bit quantized mix) with aggressive KV cache priming and request coalescing for that customer. That said, 50ms p95 is tight depending on sequence length — 50ms target is plausible for short requests (~<64 tokens) on A100/H100 class nodes with continuous batching and warmed KV. For chat/longer sequences the p95 will be higher.
- Fallback: We should offer an explicit fallback policy: primary (dedicated high-performance pool) with guaranteed p95 target, and a fallback to a lower-cost pool (same region) with a softer SLA (99.9% / p95 < 120ms) if capacity constraints occur. That gives Zephyrus a safety net and helps us limit exposure.
- Sizing: preliminary estimate — for their expected peak QPS (they provided in the brief), we'll need 6 dedicated GPUs (H100-equivalent) with an additional 2 standby nodes for 20% buffer. I attached a perf sim summary with latency distributions from our internal bench.
- Risks: model updates (rollouts) could shift tail latency; we need pinned model versions + canary velocity controls. Also, KV cache priming on day 1 may require warmup traffic or synthetic priming scripts.

Attaching perf sim CSV and a short checklist.

Aditya
Director, Product — Serving
[Attachment: perf-sim-summary.csv (CSV)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-12T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Priority latency & availability ask — Zephyrus pilot

Operational notes from infra:
- Standup/Capacity: we can provision a dedicated pool (6 active + 2 hot-standby) in us-west-2 within 72 hours given capacity reservations. Cost will be incremental and includes reserved instances + guaranteed CPU/GPU allocation.
- On-call & Runbook: we will provide a dedicated on-call rotation for the launch window (24/7 2-person coverage) and a runbook stub covering escalation paths, contact tree, and auto-scaling thresholds. I'll include SOPs for KV cache priming and a plan for synthetic warmup traffic.
- Monitoring/Alerts: need to add Zephyrus-specific dashboards and a SLO monitor that emails both our ops and Zephyrus on degradation. We can provide audit logs and request traces; retention will be per their compliance ask (TBD with legal).
- Constraints: if a broad regional outage occurs, we must be explicit about dependencies — cross-region failover will change latency guarantees and is out-of-scope for the 99.995% pledge unless we include multi-region reserved capacity.

Attaching an infra-runbook-stub.

Grace
Head of Infrastructure Operations
[Attachment: infra-runbook-stub.md (MD)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-15T10:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Priority latency & availability ask — Zephyrus pilot

Legal here — preliminary items we need before sign-off:
- Redline of proposed SLA (I can produce a first draft). We need to carve out force majeure, clear definitions for availability measurement (region, endpoints, measurement windows), and exhaustion definitions for capacity-limited failures.
- Data handling: Zephyrus must specify any data residency or deletion windows. If they require longer audit log retention or additional access for audits, that'll be a separate attachment to the MSA.
- Certifications: confirm SOC2 scope and timeline; if they require SOC2 + ISO27001 evidence we need to enumerate what we can provide and timelines for gaps.
- Credit/penalty structure: we should align commercial with finance on whether credits are acceptable vs. failure to meet SLA. Recommend a cap (e.g., credits limited to a % of monthly reserved fee) rather than unlimited exposure.

I can produce a redline SLA by 12/17 if legal has the perf/ops inputs finalized.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Matt Chen <matt.chen@zephyrus.com>, Sara Alvarez <sara.alvarez@zephyrus.com>, procurement@zephyrus.com
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-18T16:45:00Z
Subject: Zephyrus pilot — proposed scope and next steps (draft SLA attached)

Matt / Sara — thanks for the patience while we coordinated internally. Below is the proposed approach and immediate next steps so procurement/legal can proceed: 

Proposed commitments (for launch window and agreed reserved period):
- Availability: 99.995% availability for the dedicated pool in us-west-2 during the agreed launch window. Outages caused by regional cloud provider failures or cross-region failover are excluded unless we provision multi-region reserved capacity.
- Latency: Target P95 < 60ms for short-form requests (<64 tokens) on the dedicated pool. We will include an explicit fallback policy: if the dedicated pool is exhausted we fail over to an alternate pool with a softer commitment of 99.9% / P95 < 120ms. The fallback behavior will be visible to Zephyrus via the dashboard and an incident notification.
- Capacity & ops: Redwood will provision 6 active GPUs + 2 hot-standby for the initial launch week; we will provide a dedicated 24/7 on-call rotation and the infra runbook. Zephyrus will provide expected warmup traffic patterns or allow Redwood to run synthetic priming.
- Measurement & credits: availability and latency measurement methodology will be defined in the SLA. For any SLA breach, credits will apply up to X% of the reserved monthly fee (commercial terms to be negotiated).
- Compliance: we'll include SOC2 evidence and audit log retention terms in the addendum; Laura will send a redline SLA by 12/17 for your review (attached is an initial draft).

Next steps:
1) Zephyrus provides confirmation if the fallback policy is acceptable and whether multi-region capacity is required.
2) Procurement reviews the attached draft SLA and returns redlines or escalation items.
3) Redwood legal (Laura) will incorporate redlines and produce a final addendum for signatures.

Attaching: redline-sla-draft.pdf (first pass). We'll follow up with a DocuSign link once commercial terms are agreed.

Appreciate the partnership — cc'ing product/infra/legal/ops for visibility.

Best,
David Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redline-sla-draft.pdf (PDF)]
